n6d89fe3390a.s: In the present Rajya Sabha of 245 members, how many seats represent the Union Territories?
n6d89fe3390a.x: The present Rajya Sabha has 225 representatives of States, 8 of Union Territories and 12 nominated members.

nc6c1f520bae.s: Under the Tenth Schedule, disqualification on the ground of defection is decided by the:
o: Speaker or Chairman of the House
nc6c1f520bae.x: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha decides defection cases, subject to judicial review; the President does not.

n4eecb9ef37b.s: The 106th Constitutional Amendment reserves what share of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies?
n4eecb9ef37b.x: The 106th Amendment reserves one-third of the seats, not one-half, under Article 334A.

n42655f5dbae.s: What happened to the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha?
o: It was passed with the special majority
It was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
It was defeated, short of the special majority
n42655f5dbae.x: The Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha because it did not secure the special majority needed for a constitutional amendment.

nindian-polity-78-11.s: The minimum age for membership of the Lok Sabha is:
nindian-polity-78-11.x: A Lok Sabha member must be at least 25 years old; for the Rajya Sabha the minimum is 30 years.

n890ab4fb617.s: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 extended the reservation of Lok Sabha seats for SCs and STs till:
n890ab4fb617.x: The 104th Amendment extended SC/ST reservation by ten years, till 2030, and ended only the nomination of Anglo-Indians.

nindian-polity-13-6.s: Which Union Territories are represented in the Rajya Sabha?
nindian-polity-13-6.x: Among the Union Territories only Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir have Rajya Sabha seats.

nindian-polity-78-8.s: Under Article 243F(1)(a), the minimum age to contest Panchayat elections is:
nindian-polity-78-8.x: Article 243F(1)(a) prescribes 21 years for Panchayat membership, while Article 326 fixes the voting age at 18.

nfd049486ac5.s: Under Article 102, an MP is disqualified for unsoundness of mind when it is declared by:
nfd049486ac5.x: Article 102 disqualifies a member declared of unsound mind by a competent court.

n782f0d49163.s: A member's resignation from the Lok Sabha is addressed in writing to the:
n782f0d49163.x: A resignation is addressed in writing to the Speaker (or the Chairman in the Rajya Sabha), who may reject it if it is not voluntary or genuine.

na8edbdf2566.s: Which of the following pairs about qualifications for Parliament is correctly matched?
o: Domicile in the State for Rajya Sabha candidates – still required
Domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha – never existed
Candidate for Parliament – registered elector in a parliamentary constituency
Candidate for Parliament – elector only in the State he resides in
na8edbdf2566.x: A parliamentary candidate must be a registered elector in a parliamentary constituency; the Rajya Sabha domicile requirement existed but was removed in 2003.

n331a1ed8083.s: Women's representation in the Lok Sabha at present is approximately:
n331a1ed8083.x: Women are about 15 per cent of the Lok Sabha and about 14 per cent of the Rajya Sabha; one-third is the future reservation.

nindian-polity-8-25.s: When the President returns a Bill once to Parliament for reconsideration, he uses the:
nindian-polity-8-25.x: Returning a Bill once is the suspensive veto; keeping it pending is the pocket veto and withholding assent is the absolute veto.

nindian-polity-38-28.s: During a recess of Parliament, the President may promulgate ordinances under Article:
nindian-polity-38-28.x: A recess is the gap between prorogation and the next session, and the President can issue ordinances under Article 123 during it.

n9c99cd94be5.s: Which Amendment allows the Speaker or Chairman to reject a member's resignation that is not voluntary or genuine?
n9c99cd94be5.x: The 33rd Amendment Act, 1974 amended Article 101(3)(b); the 52nd added the Tenth Schedule.

nindian-polity-2-11.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
nindian-polity-2-11.x: Article 112 deals with the Annual Financial Statement; Article 93 is the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, and Article 108 the joint sitting.

n5085dcb8013.s: The Panel of Chairpersons of the Lok Sabha is nominated by the:
n5085dcb8013.x: The Speaker nominates up to ten members to the panel; one presides when both Speaker and Deputy Speaker are absent.

nindian-polity-58-20.s: The Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha addresses his resignation to the:
nindian-polity-58-20.x: The Deputy Speaker resigns to the Speaker, and the Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker, not to the President.

nindian-polity-57-3.s: Who can be chosen Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
o: Any citizen, if elected to the House within six months
A member of either House of Parliament
Only an elected member of the Lok Sabha
A Rajya Sabha member nominated by the President
nindian-polity-57-3.x: The Speaker must already be an elected Lok Sabha member; the six-month relaxation applies only to Ministers.

nindian-polity-57-17.s: The Pro-Tem Speaker of the Lok Sabha is appointed by the President under Article:
nindian-polity-57-17.x: The Pro-Tem Speaker is appointed by the President under Article 95(1); only the regular Speaker is elected under Article 93.

nindian-polity-58-16.s: Which presiding officer of the Lok Sabha does NOT vacate office when the House is dissolved?
nindian-polity-58-16.x: Only the Speaker stays in office after dissolution, till just before the new House first meets; the Deputy Speaker vacates at once.

nindian-polity-58-3.s: The practice of choosing the Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker from the Opposition rests on:
o: Rule 8(1) of the Lok Sabha Rules
nindian-polity-58-3.x: The Deputy Speaker is elected by the House from its members; picking an Opposition member is only a convention, not a constitutional requirement.

nc32529eaeda.s: While a resolution for his removal is under consideration, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha may:
o: Exercise a casting vote in a tie
nc32529eaeda.x: Under Article 96 the Speaker cannot preside during his removal resolution but may speak and vote in the first instance, though not cast a vote in a tie.

nindian-polity-57-38.s: The Speaker's certificate endorsed on a Money Bill is given under Article:
nindian-polity-57-38.x: Under Article 110(4) the Speaker certifies a Money Bill, and the certificate is final; the Rajya Sabha cannot overrule it.

nindian-polity-57-10.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about presiding officers when the Lok Sabha is dissolved?
o: The Speaker vacates office immediately on dissolution.
The Speaker continues until just before the new Lok Sabha first meets.
The Deputy Speaker vacates office at once.
A State Speaker follows the same rule under Article 179.
nindian-polity-57-10.x: The Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution; he continues until just before the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha.

ndceb51224a5.s: Which Article provides separate secretarial staff for each House of Parliament?
ndceb51224a5.x: Article 98 gives each House its own secretarial staff while permitting posts common to both Houses.

n690f2a8fefa.s: The Secretary-General of a House of Parliament is appointed by the:
n690f2a8fefa.x: The Secretary-General is appointed by the presiding officer of the House, keeping the secretariat independent of the executive.

ncbeb2036508.s: Who was the first Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council?
ncbeb2036508.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao was the first Council Chairman; Kalluri Subbarao was Deputy Speaker and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao Speaker of the first Assembly.

nf2348f7c728.s: Zero Hour, an informal Indian parliamentary innovation, has been in use since:
nf2348f7c728.x: Zero Hour dates from 1962 and is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure; 1953 and 1954 are the short-duration discussion and calling attention.

nindian-polity-34-14.s: Supplementary questions are allowed on which of the following?
nindian-polity-34-14.x: Starred and short notice questions get oral answers and allow supplementaries; unstarred questions get written answers without them.

nindian-polity-34-15.s: Which parliamentary questions are marked with an asterisk?
nindian-polity-34-15.x: Starred questions carry an asterisk; unstarred questions do not, and a short notice question is known by its shorter notice.

nindian-polity-33-19.s: Zero Hour and the Calling Attention Motion are:
o: Expressly provided for in the Constitution
Created by the Representation of the People Act, 1951
Borrowed from the British House of Commons
Indian innovations not mentioned in the Constitution
nindian-polity-33-19.x: Both grew out of Indian parliamentary practice; neither is mentioned in the Constitution, and Zero Hour is not even in the Rules.

n177b5de3d9f.s: A resolution to remove the Lok Sabha Speaker under Article 94(c) must be passed by:
o: A majority of all the then members of the House
A simple majority of members present and voting
Two-thirds of members present and voting
n177b5de3d9f.x: Removal needs a majority of all the then members (an effective majority), after 14 days' notice; a simple majority is not enough.

n3021436b15f.s: How many members does the Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges have?
n3021436b15f.x: The Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges has 15 members nominated by the Speaker; the Rajya Sabha committee has 10.

ne6abb27180a.s: A committee on a Bill made up of members of both Houses is a:
ne6abb27180a.x: A Joint Committee has members of both Houses and is formed on a motion; a Select Committee has members of one House only.

nindian-polity-55-9.s: Unlike an adjournment motion, a calling attention motion:
o: Can be moved only in the Lok Sabha
Sets aside the normal business of the House
nindian-polity-55-9.x: A calling attention motion seeks a Minister's statement without censure and is allowed in either House with the presiding officer's permission.

nindian-polity-35-29.s: How many members does the Committee on Subordinate Legislation have in each House?
nindian-polity-35-29.x: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation has 15 members in each House, and Ministers cannot sit on it.

nindian-polity-39-23.s: How many seats were contested in the first Lok Sabha general elections?
nindian-polity-39-23.x: 489 seats were contested in the first Lok Sabha elections; G.V. Mavalankar became the first Speaker.

nindian-polity-46-34.s: A Confidence Motion in the Lok Sabha is moved by the:
nindian-polity-46-34.x: The Government moves a confidence motion to prove its majority; a no-confidence motion is moved by the Opposition.

nindian-polity-55-45.s: Under which rule of the Lok Sabha is a discussion followed by a formal motion and voting held?
nindian-polity-55-45.x: Rule 184 allows a discussion ending in a formal motion and vote, and defeat on it can threaten the ruling party.

nindian-polity-38-32.s: Which of the following pairs about a no-confidence motion is correctly matched?
o: House where moved – Lok Sabha only
Rule of the Lok Sabha – Rule 184
nindian-polity-38-32.x: A no-confidence motion (Rule 198) is moved only in the Lok Sabha with 50 members' support and needs no reasons.

nb3265088933.s: Besides Question Hour and motions, State Legislatures control the executive through:
nb3265088933.x: State Legislatures use the same parliamentary devices and also estimates and public accounts committees.

nindian-polity-35-7.s: Members of the three Financial Committees of Parliament are elected for a term of:
nindian-polity-35-7.x: Members of the PAC, Estimates and Public Undertakings Committees are elected by PR-STV for one year.

nf5f6e41c9a2.s: Who among the following cannot be a member of the Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs?
o: A member of the ruling party
nf5f6e41c9a2.x: No minister can be a member of the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

nindian-polity-35-11.s: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee was made a permanent committee in:
nindian-polity-35-11.x: The Ethics Committee became permanent in 2015; it cannot take up matters pending in court.

n08f0b1332c4.s: Who decides whether a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha is admitted?
n08f0b1332c4.x: The Speaker has discretion to admit or reject a no-confidence motion; reasons need not be stated.

ncc704077bc3.s: Which of the following is a tool of parliamentary control over the executive?
ncc704077bc3.x: The half-an-hour discussion is a parliamentary device; judicial review is a function of the judiciary, not Parliament.

new.s: Under Article 59(1), if a Member of Parliament is elected President, he:
o: Gives up his seat in the House
Keeps his seat but cannot vote
Keeps his seat till the next election
new.x: Article 59(1) bars the President from being a member of either House; an MP elected President gives up his seat.

new.s: The President may address either House or both Houses together at any time under Article:
new.x: Article 86 lets the President address either or both Houses; Article 87 is the special address at the first session.

new.s: The 7th Amendment, 1956 fixed the strength of the Lok Sabha at:
new.x: The 7th Amendment, 1956 fixed the Lok Sabha at 520; the 31st Amendment, 1973 raised it from 525 to 545.

new.s: Under Article 330, Lok Sabha seats for SCs and STs were reserved initially for:
new.x: Article 330 reserved SC/ST seats in proportion to population, first for 10 years, and it has been repeatedly extended.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the strength of the Lok Sabha?
o: The First Lok Sabha had 489 elected seats.
new.x: 552 was the old maximum that counted 2 Anglo-Indian nominees; the present maximum is 550.

new.s: Who was the first woman nominated to the Rajya Sabha (1952)?
new.x: Rukmini Devi Arundale was the first nominated woman (1952); Nargis Dutt was the first film actress nominee (1980).

new.s: A nominated member of the Rajya Sabha may join a political party within what period of taking his seat without disqualification?
new.x: A nominated member may join a party within 6 months; after that he is disqualified under the Tenth Schedule.

new.s: Members of the Rajya Sabha from the States are elected by the:
o: Single transferable vote by all MLAs and MLCs
Majority vote of the Lok Sabha
Single transferable vote by elected MLAs
new.x: Under Article 80(4) elected MLAs choose Rajya Sabha members by PR-STV; nominated MLAs and MLCs cannot vote.

new.s: Which sportsperson was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 2016?
new.x: Mary Kom was nominated in 2016 and Sachin Tendulkar in 2012, though sport is not a field listed in Article 80(3).

new.s: Which State has 12 seats in the Rajya Sabha?
new.x: Karnataka has 12 Rajya Sabha seats, followed by Gujarat 11, Odisha 10 and Kerala 9.

new.s: Undivided Andhra Pradesh's 18 Rajya Sabha seats were split after 2014 as:
new.x: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended the Fourth Schedule: AP got 11 and Telangana 7 Rajya Sabha seats.

new.s: How many seats does Andhra Pradesh have in its Legislative Assembly?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh has a 175-member Assembly, 25 Lok Sabha and 11 Rajya Sabha seats; Telangana's Assembly has 119.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (State – Rajya Sabha seats) is correctly matched?
new.x: West Bengal and Bihar have 16 each; Maharashtra has 19, Tamil Nadu 18 and Uttar Pradesh 31.

new.s: Which is the smallest Lok Sabha constituency by area?
new.x: Chandni Chowk in Delhi (10.59 sq km) is the smallest by area; Lakshadweep is the smallest by number of electors.

new.s: Which is the largest Lok Sabha constituency by number of electors?
new.x: Malkajgiri in Telangana has the most electors; Ladakh is the largest by area.

new.s: Which is the smallest Lok Sabha constituency by number of electors?
new.x: Lakshadweep has the fewest electors, while Chandni Chowk is the smallest by area.

new.s: During a National Emergency, an extension of the Lok Sabha cannot continue beyond how long after the Emergency ends?
new.x: The term can be extended by law one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ends.

new.s: Which of the following Lok Sabhas was NOT dissolved before completing its term?
new.x: The 4th, 6th, 9th, 11th, 12th and 13th Lok Sabhas were dissolved early; the 14th is not among them.

new.s: A member elected to a casual vacancy in the Rajya Sabha serves for:
o: The rest of the predecessor's term
new.x: A casual vacancy in the Rajya Sabha is filled for the remainder of the term only.

new.s: What educational qualification does the Constitution prescribe for membership of Parliament?
new.x: No educational qualification is laid down; lack of a degree is not a ground of disqualification either.

new.s: The highest minimum entry age in the Constitution, 35 years, applies to the:
new.x: 35 years is required for the President, Vice-President and Governor; 30 is for the Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council.

new.s: Rajya Sabha candidates had to be domiciled in the State they represented only until:
new.x: The domicile requirement applied only before 6 April 2003; its removal was upheld in Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006).

new.s: The term 'office of profit' is defined in:
o: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
Neither the Constitution nor the RPA
new.x: 'Office of profit' is not defined in the Constitution or the RPA; exempted posts are listed in the 1959 Act.

new.s: Which case held that the Speaker's decisions under the Tenth Schedule are subject to judicial review?
new.x: Kihoto Hollohan (1992) upheld the Speaker's or Chairman's role in defection cases, subject to judicial review.

new.s: A person elected to both Houses of Parliament who does not choose one within 10 days loses his seat in the:
o: House he was elected to first
new.x: If he does not choose within 10 days, his Rajya Sabha seat falls vacant; for Parliament plus a State the limit is 14 days.

new.s: If a person is elected to two seats in the Lok Sabha and does not choose one, then:
new.x: A member elected to two seats in one House must choose one; otherwise both seats fall vacant.

new.s: Which Lok Sabha recorded the highest number of women members, 78?
new.x: The 17th Lok Sabha (2019) had 78 women (14.36%), the highest; the 18th (2024) has 74.

new.s: The 106th Amendment's women's reservation is governed by Article:
new.x: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam reserves one-third seats under Article 334A for 15 years, after the next Census and delimitation.

new.s: The Women's Reservation Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha in:
new.x: The first Bill came in 1996, it was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010, and the 106th Amendment came in 2023.

new.s: How many minimum sitting days a year does the Constitution prescribe for Parliament?
new.x: Article 85 fixes only the six-month maximum gap between sessions; it prescribes no minimum number of sitting days.

new.s:
Arrange in order after the business of a session ends:
1. Recess
2. Prorogation
3. Adjournment sine die
4. New session
new.x: Adjournment sine die by the presiding officer comes first, then prorogation by the President, then recess, then a new session.

new.s: Which House can be dissolved?
new.x: Dissolution ends the House and applies only to the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha is permanent.

new.s: Freedom from civil arrest of an MP extends to how many days before and after a session?
new.x: Members cannot be arrested in civil cases during a session and 40 days before and after it; criminal cases are not covered.

new.s: The Sita Soren judgment (2024) overruled which earlier decision on bribery and privilege?
new.x: A seven-judge Bench in Sita Soren (2024) held there is no privilege for a bribe to vote or speak, overruling P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998).

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a collective privilege of a House of Parliament?
o: Being informed of a member's arrest
new.x: Exemption from jury service is an individual privilege of members; the others belong to the House collectively.

new.s: Which of the following can be done only by the Lok Sabha?
new.x: Only the Lok Sabha can discontinue a National Emergency; both Houses approve emergencies and take part in impeachment and removal of judges.

new.s: In the Budget process, the Rajya Sabha cannot:
o: Make recommendations on a Money Bill
new.x: The Rajya Sabha may discuss the Budget but cannot vote on demands for grants, which is a Lok Sabha power.

new.s: A proceeding to remove the Vice-President can be started only in the Rajya Sabha under Article:
new.x: Under Article 67(b) a resolution to remove the Vice-President can begin only in the Rajya Sabha.

new.s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 remains in force for:
o: Until the Lok Sabha is dissolved
new.x: An Article 249 resolution is valid for one year and can be renewed one year at a time.

new.s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 authorises which body to make laws on a State List subject?
new.x: Article 249 empowers Parliament, not State Assemblies, to legislate on a State List matter in the national interest.

new.s: Parliament makes a law for two or more States on the resolutions of their legislatures under Article:
new.x: Under Article 252 Parliament legislates for consenting States; other States may adopt that law later.

new.s: Parliament can legislate on any subject to implement international treaties under Article:
new.x: Article 253 lets Parliament make laws to implement international treaties and agreements.

new.s: The Rajya Sabha elects which of its presiding officers?
new.x: The Rajya Sabha elects only its Deputy Chairman; the Vice-President is its ex officio Chairman.

new.s: A notice to impeach the President must be signed by at least what fraction of the members of the House?
new.x: The impeachment notice must be signed by one-fourth of the members and given 14 days in advance.

new.s: If the Lok Sabha were enlarged by about 50%, the Lok Sabha-to-Rajya Sabha ratio would change from 2.2:1 to about:
new.x: Raising the Lok Sabha to about 815 would push the ratio with the Rajya Sabha from 2.2:1 to 3.3:1.

new.s: With an enlarged Lok Sabha of about 815, the 15% cap on the Council of Ministers would rise from 81 to about:
new.x: The 15% ministerial cap would rise from 81 to about 122.

new.s: A resolution to remove the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is provided under Article:
new.x: Article 90(c) provides for removal of the Deputy Chairman by an effective majority of the Rajya Sabha after 14 days' notice.

new.s: For the removal of which of the following is 14 days' notice NOT required?
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
new.x: The Governor is removed by the President at will without notice; the President, Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Deputy Chairman need 14 days' notice.

new.s: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha can be removed from office only:
o: By a two-thirds vote of the Rajya Sabha
new.x: The Vice-President is ex officio Chairman, so he leaves the Chair only on removal as Vice-President.

new.s: Under Article 179, the rule that the Speaker continues after dissolution applies to:
o: The Speaker of a State Assembly
The Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of a Legislative Council
new.x: Article 179 lays down the same rule for the State Speaker, who also continues till just before the new Assembly first meets.

new.s: During consideration of a resolution for his own removal, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
o: May vote in the first instance
new.x: The Chairman cannot preside or vote during his own removal resolution but may speak; the Speaker, by contrast, can vote in the first instance.

new.s: The tenure of the Pro-Tem Speaker ends when:
new.x: The Pro-Tem Speaker administers oath and holds the Speaker's election; his role ends once the regular Speaker is elected.

new.s: The list of senior members for appointing the Pro-Tem Speaker is sent to the:
new.x: The President appoints the senior-most member as Pro-Tem Speaker; the list of senior members goes to the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs.

new.s: The Speaker's power to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill is given by Article:
new.x: Article 110(3) makes the Speaker's decision on a Money Bill final; the certificate is endorsed under 110(4).

new.s: The post of Leader of the Opposition was given statutory status by an Act of:
new.x: The Speaker recognises the LoP if the party has one-tenth of the House; the office became statutory under the 1977 Act.

new.s: The Speaker presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses under Article:
new.x: The President summons a joint sitting under Article 108, and the Speaker presides under Article 118(4).

new.s: When the Deputy Speaker is appointed to a parliamentary committee, he:
o: Needs the Speaker's approval to attend
new.x: The Deputy Speaker automatically becomes the chairman of any committee he is appointed to.

new.s: In the Rajya Sabha, the counterpart of the Lok Sabha's Panel of Chairpersons is the:
new.x: The Rajya Sabha has a Panel of Vice-Chairpersons nominated by the Chairman.

new.s: Which State Assembly's Deputy Speaker post had been vacant for 21 years by June 2026?
new.x: The Deputy Speaker post was vacant in 8 State Assemblies, and in Jharkhand for 21 years, as of June 2026.

new.s: Who was the first Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
new.x: S. Radhakrishnan was the first Chairman (1952–62); C.P. Radhakrishnan is the present Chairman.

new.s: When the Vice-President acts as President, he draws the salary of the:
new.x: While acting as President, the Vice-President draws the President's salary, and the Deputy Chairman does the Chairman's work under Article 91.

new.s: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha has:
o: An ordinary vote in all divisions
A vote only on Money Bills
new.x: The Vice-President, as ex officio Chairman, is not a member of the Rajya Sabha and has only a casting vote.

new.s: Who was the first elected Speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly (1925)?
new.x: Vithalbhai Patel was the first elected Speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly (1925–30).

new.s: Who is known as the 'Father of the Lok Sabha'?
new.x: G.V. Mavalankar, the first Lok Sabha Speaker (1952–56), is called the Father of the Lok Sabha.

new.s: Who was the second woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
new.x: Sumitra Mahajan (16th Lok Sabha, 2014–19) was the second woman Speaker after Meira Kumar.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Speaker – year of failed removal motion) is correctly matched?
new.x: Failed removal motions were against Mavalankar (1954), Hukum Singh (1966) and Balram Jakhar (1987); the Om Birla motion was rejected in March 2026.

new.s: The quorum of a House of Parliament is fixed by Article:
new.x: Article 100(3) fixes the quorum at one-tenth of total members, including the presiding officer.

new.s: Which session of Parliament is usually the longest?
new.x: The Budget Session (February–May) is the longest; the three sessions are a convention, not in the Constitution.

new.s: The six-month rule for sessions of State Legislatures is laid down in Article:
new.x: Article 174 applies the same six-month maximum gap to State Legislatures.

new.s: Prorogation of the Lok Sabha is done by the President under Article:
new.x: Article 85(2)(a) empowers the President to prorogue; 85(2)(b) is dissolution.

new.s: The President prorogues the Houses of Parliament on the advice of the:
new.x: Prorogation is done by the President on the Council of Ministers' advice (the Governor in States); it ends the session, not the House.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Speaker's salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. The Speaker takes a separate oath of office as Speaker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Speaker's salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund (Art 97), but there is no separate oath for the Speaker, only the oath as an MP.

new.s: An adjournment sine die of the Lok Sabha is ordered by the:
new.x: Adjournment and adjournment sine die are done by the presiding officer; prorogation and dissolution by the President.

new.s: What happens to pending bills on adjournment sine die of a House?
o: They go to a joint sitting
They are sent to the President
new.x: Adjournment sine die precedes prorogation and pending bills continue (APPSC 2025); bills lapse only on dissolution.

new.s: The President's special address under Article 87 is made at the first session of each year and the first session after:
new.x: Article 87 requires a special address at the first session after each general election and of each year, not after every prorogation.

new.s: Under Article 86, besides addressing the Houses the President may:
new.x: Article 86 lets the President address either or both Houses, require members' attendance and send messages on pending Bills.

new.s: The Secretary-General of each House of Parliament holds a rank equal to the:
new.x: The Secretary-General, appointed by the presiding officer, holds the rank of the Cabinet Secretary.

new.s: The idea of a separate secretariat for the legislature was raised in 1926 by:
new.x: Vithalbhai Patel, Speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly, raised the separate secretariat idea in 1926.

new.s: Parliamentary control over the Council of Ministers flows mainly from Article:
new.x: Article 75(3) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, the basis of parliamentary devices of control.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Indian parliamentary innovations:
1. The short-duration discussion was introduced in 1953.
2. The calling attention motion was introduced in 1962.
3. Zero Hour is not mentioned in the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The short-duration discussion dates from 1953 and Zero Hour (1962) is not in the Constitution; calling attention came in 1954, not 1962.

new.s: In the Lok Sabha, Question Hour is held during:
new.x: Question Hour is the first hour in the Lok Sabha, 11 AM to 12 Noon; Zero Hour follows from 12 Noon.

new.s: Notice for an ordinary question in Parliament must be given at least:
new.x: Ordinary questions need 15 clear days' notice; a short notice question is given with less than 10 days' notice.

new.s: The formal right of members to ask questions of the Executive is called:
new.x: Interpellation is the formal right of asking questions of the Executive.

new.s: Directions given by the Chair during Zero Hour reach the ministry concerned through the:
new.x: The Chair's directions in Zero Hour go through the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs to the ministry concerned.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (question – colour of paper) is correctly matched?
o: Question to a private member – Blue
new.x: Short notice questions are on light pink paper; starred are green, unstarred white and questions to private members yellow.

new.s: A White Paper is:
o: A report of the Committee on Petitions
An official Government document explaining its policy on a subject
The record of Zero Hour proceedings
new.x: A White Paper is an official Government document explaining policy on a subject, often to gather views before a bill.

new.s: A short-duration discussion under Rule 193 can last at most:
new.x: A Rule 193 discussion lasts at most 2 hours and has no vote, unlike Rule 184.

new.s: 'Special Mentions' in the Rajya Sabha are made under:
new.x: Special Mentions in the Rajya Sabha come under Rules 180A–E; Rule 377 is the Lok Sabha equivalent for other matters.

new.s: The no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha is moved under:
new.x: Rule 198 governs the no-confidence motion; Rule 222 is the privilege motion and Rule 184 a discussion with vote.

new.s: A matter under Rule 377 is raised after written notice to the Secretary-General and the consent of the:
new.x: Rule 377 matters need written notice to the Secretary-General and the Speaker's consent.

new.s: The debate on an admitted Adjournment Motion must last at least:
new.x: An adjournment motion suspends normal business, and its debate lasts at least 2 hours 30 minutes.

new.s: How many adjournment motions can be taken up in a single sitting?
new.x: Only one adjournment motion is allowed per sitting, on a definite matter of recent occurrence.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of an Adjournment Motion?
o: It is moved only in the Lok Sabha.
It can raise a question of privilege.
It needs the support of 50 members.
It involves an element of censure.
new.x: An adjournment motion cannot raise a question of privilege; it is a Lok Sabha device needing 50 members and carries censure.

new.s: If a censure motion against a minister is passed, the minister:
new.x: A censure motion expresses disapproval of policy; unlike a no-confidence motion, it does not force resignation.

new.s: The no-confidence motion against the Prakasam ministry of Andhra State (1954) was carried by:
new.x: Gouthu Latchanna's motion passed 69–68 and the Prakasam ministry fell by one vote after 13 months.

new.s: A no-confidence motion is directed against:
new.x: A no-confidence motion is against the whole Council of Ministers; if passed, the whole CoM must resign.

new.s: Notice of a no-confidence motion is given in writing to the:
new.x: Written notice goes to the Secretary-General, and at least 50 members must support leave to move it.

new.s: A token cut motion reduces a demand for grant by:
new.x: A token cut reduces the demand by Rs 100 to air a specific grievance; a policy cut reduces it to Re 1.

new.s: A privilege motion against a Minister for withholding or distorting facts can be moved in:
new.x: A privilege motion can be moved in either House with the presiding officer's consent and does not force resignation.

new.s: A resolution moved in Parliament can be withdrawn by its mover only with the:
o: Consent of the Business Advisory Committee
new.x: A resolution is a substantive motion that must be put to vote; the mover cannot withdraw it without leave of the House.

new.s: A three-line whip directs members to:
o: Vote strictly as the party directs
new.x: A one-line whip informs, a two-line whip directs attendance and a three-line whip is a strict voting direction.

new.s: In February 2026, the AP Legislative Council was adjourned amid a row over which issue?
new.x: The AP Legislative Council was adjourned in February 2026 amid a Question Hour / short-duration discussion row on the Tirumala laddu issue.

new.s: The closure in which only important clauses are debated and the rest are taken as passed is:
new.x: Kangaroo closure debates only the important clauses; the guillotine puts undiscussed clauses to vote when time ends.

new.s: A point of order raised in the House:
o: Allows no debate and is ruled on by the presiding officer
Is followed by a full debate
Is referred to the Rules Committee
new.x: A point of order is raised when proceedings depart from the rules; there is no debate and the presiding officer rules on it.

new.s: How many members does the Public Accounts Committee have?
new.x: The PAC has 22 members, 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha; 30 from the Lok Sabha only is the Estimates Committee.

new.s: The Estimates Committee took its present form in 1950 on the recommendation of:
new.x: The Estimates Committee dates from 1921 and took its present form in 1950 on John Mathai's recommendation; Krishna Menon is linked to COPU.

new.s: Who headed the Public Accounts Committee of the 18th Lok Sabha?
new.x: K.C. Venugopal heads the PAC of the 18th Lok Sabha (also for 2026–27).

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a financial committee of Parliament?
o: Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of MPs
new.x: The Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of MPs is not a financial committee; the PAC, Estimates and COPU are.

new.s: How many Department-related Standing Committees are there?
new.x: There are 24 DRSCs, 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha, each with 31 members.

new.s: Each Department-related Standing Committee has how many members?
new.x: Each DRSC has 31 members, 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha, with a quorum of 11.

new.s: Which committee examines whether Ministers' promises in the House are implemented?
o: Committee on Papers Laid on the Table
new.x: The Committee on Government Assurances watches Ministers' promises till they are implemented.

new.s: The Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee was constituted in:
new.x: The Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee was set up on 4 March 1997; the Lok Sabha had an ad hoc one in 2000, made permanent in 2015.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (committee – reform area) is correctly matched?
new.x: Nachiket Mor is linked to financial inclusion; Shanta Kumar to FCI/PDS, Kasturirangan to NEP 2020 and Urjit Patel to inflation targeting.

new.s: What share of Bills was referred to parliamentary committees in the 15th Lok Sabha?
new.x: 71% of Bills went to committees in the 15th Lok Sabha, against only 16% in the 17th.

new.s: In the 17th Lok Sabha, Question Hour functioned for about what share of its scheduled time?
new.x: Question Hour ran only about 60% of its time in the 17th Lok Sabha.
